display_name: Mahmud Khalji I & Rana Kumbha (Battle of Sarangpur)
one_line: Rivals in the Mewar–Malwa frontier wars, clashing at Sarangpur and over Chittorgarh’s prestige.

appearance.age_look: Mahmud: early 40s, lean and sharp; Kumbha: late 30s, tall and broad-shouldered.
appearance.face: Mahmud has an angular face, medium-brown Malwa complexion, hawk-like nose, neatly trimmed beard and moustache, intense narrow eyes with a calculating frown; Kumbha has a square jaw, wheatish Rajput complexion, straight nose, short trimmed moustache and light stubble, large determined eyes with a calm, resolute gaze.
appearance.hair: Mahmud’s dark brown hair is hidden under a tall cylindrical quilted cap wrapped in deep green cloth with a narrow gold band; Kumbha’s straight dark hair is shoulder-length, oiled and combed back from the forehead, partly covered by a simple padded cotton turban in muted saffron with a thin white stripe.
appearance.costume: Mahmud wears a long knee-length quilted jama in rich dark teal cotton with fine vertical stitching, tied to the side with a maroon sash, over mail hinted at the collar, paired with fitted cream churidar trousers and brown leather riding boots; over his jama he has a short sleeveless maroon overcoat with simple gold piping and a narrow leather belt with a small dagger sheath; Kumbha wears a full-sleeved ankle-length cotton angarkha in off-white with a faint block-printed geometric pattern in light brown, the overlap tied with fabric cords, over a sturdy quilted cotton waistcoat in muted indigo and a broad crimson cloth belt at the waist, with straight brown cotton trousers and simple dark leather shoes, plus a plain steel arm-guard on his left forearm and a modest beaded necklace of dark wooden beads.
appearance.signature: Mahmud carries a slightly curved Indo-Persian sabre with a steel blade, cross-guard and a dark wood hilt, sheathed at his left hip; Rana Kumbha carries a long straight steel sword with a traditional disc pommel and simple cross-guard held in his right hand, its plain scabbard of dark brown leather hanging from his crimson cloth belt.

ref_desc: Mahmud Khalji I has a dark teal quilted jama, maroon overcoat, green-wrapped tall cap and curved sabre, while Rana Kumbha wears an off-white patterned angarkha, indigo waistcoat, saffron turban, crimson belt and straight disc-pommel sword in a dark brown scabbard.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two historically grounded 15th-century Indian rivals from the Mewar–Malwa frontier: Mahmud Khalji I and Rana Kumbha standing side by side. Mahmud is lean, early-40s, medium-brown complexion with an angular face, hawk-like nose, neatly trimmed beard and moustache, and intense narrow eyes in a calculating frown; he wears a knee-length dark teal quilted cotton jama over subtle mail, tied with a maroon sash, fitted cream churidar trousers, brown leather riding boots, and a short sleeveless maroon overcoat with simple gold piping and a narrow leather belt holding a small dagger sheath. His hair is hidden by a tall cylindrical quilted cap wrapped in deep green cloth with a narrow gold band. At his left hip hangs his signature slightly curved Indo-Persian sabre with steel blade and dark wood hilt in a plain dark brown scabbard. Beside him, Rana Kumbha is tall and broad-shouldered, late-30s, wheatish complexion with a square jaw, straight nose, short trimmed moustache, light stubble and large determined eyes with a calm, resolute expression. His straight dark hair is shoulder-length, combed back, partially covered by a simple padded cotton turban in muted saffron with a thin white stripe. He wears a full-sleeved ankle-length off-white cotton angarkha with a faint light brown geometric block print, tied at the overlap, over a sturdy muted indigo quilted waistcoat, a broad crimson cloth belt, straight brown cotton trousers and dark leather shoes, plus a plain steel arm-guard on his left forearm and a modest dark wooden bead necklace. His signature weapon is a long straight steel sword with a traditional disc pommel and simple cross-guard, held in his right hand, its plain dark brown leather scabbard hanging from his crimson belt. Use a palette of dark teal, maroon, cream, muted saffron, indigo and rich brown, and show them clearly head-to-toe for consistent redrawing.
